findings.title: Round-trip test asserts policy match rather than full `ServerConfig` equality
findings.description: Success criterion 5 has two halves: (a) `config_to_yaml` emits the policy as a plain string, and (b) reloading the emitted YAML produces an *equal `ServerConfig`*. The task's `test_bounds_policy_yaml_round_trip` covers the reload and asserts the policy matches, which substantively proves the policy field round-trips, but it stops short of asserting whole-config equality. Asserting `reloaded == original` on the `ServerConfig` would cost one line and fully satisfy criterion 5. Non-blocking.

findings.title: Shipped-config defaults verified by one-off commands, not a committed regression test
findings.description: Success criterion 12 (`default.yaml` and `test.yaml` use `policy: wrap`) is verified in Tasks 4.1/4.2 via inline `python -c` load checks, which satisfies the criterion as written. There is no committed test pinning the shipped configs to `wrap`, so a later accidental edit to those YAML files would only surface in the manual walkthrough (Task 5.2). This is optional hardening, not a gap against the stated criteria — noted for the record only.
